title: The Production of Nanocellulose from Organic Waste and its Assessment Through Spectroscopic and Microscopic Methods
content: The process of utilization of organic waste as a substantial material for the economic growth and their utilization to fabricate a potential and high efficiency product is still a great challenge. The technological evolution and the development of nanotechnology-based products offers a wide possibility with unique properties for various fields of applications. Cellulose is recognized as the most prevalent biopolymer on the planet and serves as the primary component of the plant cell wall. It is a linear polysaccharide formed by extensive chains of glucose units connected via β-1,4-glycosidic bonds, resulting in a structure that features both semicrystalline and amorphous regions [1,3]. It’s remarkable mechanical strength, thermal stability, and biodegradability have facilitated its application across various industries, including the production of paper, textiles, and bioplastics [2].
